best_for: Photographers and families with a large photo archive on disk or a NAS who want to tag, rate, find faces and edit, all on their own computer with no cloud account.
description:
digiKam is a photo manager made by the digiKam team as part of the KDE community. The team says the app has no tracking or telemetry and keeps your photos, metadata and settings on your own computer.

Plug in a camera or card and digiKam can rename and rotate the shots as they come in, or convert raw files to DNG. Its duplicate finder compares image fingerprints, and you can type a search as a plain sentence. Put two similar shots side by side on the light table to pick the better one. When you are done, turn a set of photos into a calendar, a panorama, a web gallery or a video slideshow. Video files can be cataloged next to your photos.

points.title: Built for big libraries
points.text: Photos stay in your folders, on local, removable or network drives, and digiKam indexes them in a database. SQLite works out of the box; MariaDB on a server suits shared or very large collections.

points.title: Faces found on your machine
points.text: Face detection and recognition run with AI models stored locally, optionally on the GPU through OpenCV. Your photos are not sent anywhere to be tagged.

points.title: Tags, labels and maps
points.text: Add tags, captions, star ratings, color labels and pick flags, fix dates, and place photos on a map with the geolocation editor.

points.title: An editor and a batch queue
points.text: Crop, curves, levels, white balance, noise reduction, lens correction and more, with 16-bit color and versioning that keeps the original. The Batch Queue Manager runs the same steps across many files at once. Raw files are read with LibRaw.

points.title: Free, no strings
points.text: digiKam is a KDE project under GPL-2.0 or later. No account, no subscription.

points.title: Mac and Linux details
points.text: There are separate .pkg installers for Apple silicon (macOS 11.3 or later) and Intel (macOS 10.15 or later, still a Qt5 build). The Homebrew cask is disabled for failing Apple's Gatekeeper check. The Linux Flatpak is verified on Flathub; the project itself publishes an AppImage that needs glibc 2.31 or later.

points.title: Windows is all users only
points.text: The Windows installer is x64 for Windows 10 or later and installs for all users. The Windows listing keeps 18 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
